name: Acklins & Crooked Island
line: The Bight of Acklins bonefish flats

jewels.name: Bight of Acklins
jewels.blurb: "Acklins & Crooked Island curve around a 1,000 square foot lagoon known as The Bight. The water here is shallow, often no deeper than knee-height, even 5 miles off-shore. The conditions are an angler's dream." (The same page elsewhere calls it "a 500-square-mile lagoon"; the two figures are the official site's own and disagree.)
jewels.booking_route: none needed - open water; fished with a lodge guide or DIY

jewels.name: Crooked Island Lodge & Marina
jewels.blurb: "The Crooked Island Lodge has 8 air-conditioned guest rooms located just steps from white sand beaches, a private 3500' runway and an authentic local restaurant and bar"; at the northern tip of Crooked Island overlooking Bird Rock Lighthouse; 8 hotel rooms and 6 cottages, "All Doubles ~~~ $395 per night *10% VAT tax" (https://www.crookedislandlodge.com/lodge, accessed 2026-10-03). "Come enjoy the Bahamas as it was 40 years ago."
jewels.booking_route: own website form or email info@crookedislandlodge.com; 242-478-8989 or 242-478-8180

jewels.name: Acklins Creekside Bonefish Lodge
jewels.blurb: Founded by natives of Acklins at Chester's Bay: "Just 50 paces from your bed, you can step into a three-mile, ankle-to-knee-deep flat for kayaking, wading, and DIY bone fishing" (bahamas.com). Own site: the lodge "accommodates twenty persons maximum"; "Two/2 persons Double Occupancy $157.00 Per Night + 15% gratuity + 10% VAT + 8% energy surcharge"; guided bonefish day "$650.00 (two/2 share boat/guide)" (https://acklinscreeksidebonefishlodge.com/, accessed 2026-10-03).
jewels.booking_route: own website booking ("Reservation must be made direct via our hotel or our website") or (242) 357-4179

jewels.name: Crooked & Acklins Island Trophy Lodge
jewels.blurb: "Our small, quiet and private lodge is located off the beaten track on a white sandy beach, and is managed by a very friendly Bahamian couple. It has five large double rooms"; "This is the only lodge in the entire atoll which provides fishing opportunities from both islands -- Crooked and Acklins -- on the same trip, with just a 15-minute transfer by car on both sides." Winding Bay, Major's Cay, Crooked Island; owners Jean-Paul Tissieres & Herle Hamon.
jewels.booking_route: phone/email only ((242) 344-2136, contact@crookedandacklinstrophylodge.com); also sold as packages by Aardvark McLeod and Fish Partner

jewels.name: Bird Rock Lighthouse
jewels.blurb: "This magnificent structure stands 112 feet above sea level and is situated on a cay just off Pittstown Point, accessible only by boat." "Construction of the lighthouse started in 1866, and it became operational in 1876." "Chartered boat tours to the island can be arranged through Crooked Island Lodge, Scavella Enterprises, and/or local fishing guides."
jewels.booking_route: none needed to view; a boat trip is arranged through Crooked Island Lodge, Scavella Enterprises or local guides

jewels.name: Crooked Island Marina
jewels.blurb: "Our new 35 slip marina offers dockage for vessels to 160' with 10' mean low water depths throughout. We are located at Pitts Town Point near the 112' tall Bird Rock Light House, making us a perfect stopping off point for all trips north and south to the Turks and Caicos, Dominican Republic, Puerto Rico and beyond." Two fuel docks, six pumps, "dawn to dusk daily"; "Acceptable forms of payment are Visa and Mastercard only."
jewels.booking_route: VHF channel 16 on arrival; reservations by email info@crookedislandlodge.com

jewels.name: Turtle Sound
jewels.blurb: "One of the natural wonders of The Bahamas, with incredible blue-green water and an abundance of turtles, this beautiful waterway is often referred to as an inland river. It runs from the eastern end of the French Wells Channel, nine miles inland to just behind the Moss Town and Seaview settlements." "a perfect setting for all types of soft adventure or fly fishing."
jewels.booking_route: none needed - natural waterway; Crooked Island Lodge arranges trips to Turtle Sound on request

jewels.name: Pompey Bay Beach
jewels.blurb: "Pompey Bay Beach in Acklins is the site of one of the largest Lucayan settlements in The Bahamas." Wikipedia places it "just south of Spring Point" (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acklins, accessed 2026-10-03).
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free public beach

jewels.name: Grey's Point Bonefish Inn
jewels.blurb: "located in the heart of Acklins' fishing grounds. There are bonefish flats adjacent to the property and you can cast a fishing line just a few steps outside your room." "we can arrange deep-sea and reef fishing trips on our 23-foot sport fisherman boat. Packages are available that include fishing, accommodations, meals/soft drinks and airport transfers." Contact Mr. Newton Williamson.
jewels.booking_route: phone/email only ((242) 344-3210, greyspoint@hotmail.com)

jewels.name: Crooked Island offshore, flats and inshore fishing
jewels.blurb: "Blue and White Marlin abound and catches of 4-5 per day are not uncommon. Our Marlin fishery is strictly catch and release." "The flats fishing on the south side of Crooked Island has the friendliest bonefish found anywhere. The average bonefish is around three to four pounds". "The lodge works with a talented group of local guides".
jewels.booking_route: through Crooked Island Lodge (email info@crookedislandlodge.com; 242-478-8989)

jewels.name: Wall diving and The Dungeons
jewels.blurb: "Enjoy one of the closest and shallowest walls in the Caribbean at 200 yards and 33 feet to the Dungeons one of our most spectacular dives." "Walk right out of your lodgings, onto the beach and into our crystal clear waters."
jewels.booking_route: through Crooked Island Lodge (email info@crookedislandlodge.com)

jewels.name: Creekside guided bonefishing (Terrance and Elvis)
jewels.blurb: "Our guides Terrance and his brother Elvis will be delighted to teach you how to fly fish and tie fly as they accompany you at the crack of dawn to master bone-fish flats." "Bone-fishing flats are untouched in this area with an average weight of 4-9 pound fish." "FULLY GUIDED BONE FISH DAY (Guides daily tips NOT included) $650.00 (two/2 share boat/guide)".
jewels.booking_route: own website booking or (242) 357-4179

jewels.name: Long Cay
jewels.blurb: "Long Cay was originally called Fortune Island by Christopher Columbus, because he found a conch pearl when he first arrived there." Home to the first jail in the islands, "the first port of entry in the southern Bahamas", once "4,000 residents, but today has a very small population that is sometimes less than 50 persons"; St. David & St. Augustines Church; "flamingos flock on the banks of the south shore".
jewels.booking_route: none needed - reached by the daily ferry into Cabbage Hill or private boat

jewels.name: Castle Island Lighthouse
jewels.blurb: "Remote Castle Island, off the southernmost tip of Acklins, has a conspicuous 1867 lighthouse once used as the retreat of pirates who attacked ships in the nearby passage. The lighthouse is approximately five miles away from the main settlement of Salina Point. A boat is required to get to the island."
jewels.booking_route: none needed to view; a boat is required

jewels.name: Pitts Town Point private runway (MYCP)
jewels.blurb: "Crooked Island Lodge and Marina owns and operates its own 3500' runway, parking, and hangars"; paved, "3500' long by 40' wide"; "Landing fee and parking is waived for pilots and passengers arriving for boats staying at the marina or overnight lodge guests. All others, $125 landing fee, plus $75/night parking." "No aviation fuel is available and there is no customs or immigration on Crooked Island."
jewels.booking_route: Unicom 122.8 and the airport release form by email to info@crookedislandlodge.com

jewels.name: Cascarilla bark harvest
jewels.blurb: "Acklins Island is one of only two islands in The Bahamas where Cascarilla Bark grows. The bitter herb has long been used in traditional Bush Medicine. Today, it's harvested and exported as the main ingredient in Campari Liquor."
jewels.booking_route: none - no tour or seller is named on the page

jewels.name: Samana Cay Lucayan sites
jewels.blurb: "Ten ancient Lucayan sites have been unearthed by National Geographic Society Archeologists in Samana Cay alone." Wikipedia places Samana Cay "northeast of Spring Point in Acklins" (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acklins, accessed 2026-10-03).
jewels.booking_route: none - no access route or operator is named on the page

jewels.name: Plana Cays
jewels.blurb: "The Plana Cays, two small islands east of Mason's Bay, Acklins, are a protected reserve for endangered great iguanas and the very rare hutias (guinea pig like rodents), the only native mammal of The Bahamas."
jewels.booking_route: none - a protected reserve; no visitor access route is given

jewels.name: Landrail Point
jewels.blurb: "This northern port was the site of The Islands of The Bahamas first General Post Office. Its remaining walls are now part of the Crooked Island Lodge at Pittstown Point."
jewels.booking_route: none needed - public settlement

jewels.name: Conch Schell's Restaurant & Lounge
jewels.blurb: "The beachfront restaurant and lounge offer a traditional Bahamian menu. We have Native Nights on the beach some weekends, with a fish fry and Rake & Scrape music." At the Trophy Lodge, Winding Bay, Major's Cay, Crooked Island.

jewels.name: Crooked Island Lodge Restaurant & Sunset Bar & Grill
jewels.blurb: "The main lodge of this remote island resort on Crooked Island's northwestern tip was once The Bahamas' first post-office; it now functions as a restaurant, bar, and library." The lodge: the Sunset Bar & Grill has "an incredible view of Bird Rock Lighthouse"; restaurant open "for Breakfast, Lunch, and Dinner, daily by reservation. Dinner reservations must be made by 12pm each day" (https://www.crookedislandlodge.com/services, accessed 2026-10-03).
jewels.booking_route: phone/email reservation ((242) 344-2507 on the official listing; info@crookedislandlodge.com)

jewels.name: JuNette's Cafe & Club House
jewels.blurb: At Acklins Creekside Bonefish Lodge: "You can dine onsite at JuNette's Café & Club House, where our guests say, 'The food is awesome!'" The lodge's own site lists meals "@) $100 per person per day (prepared/served to order in/from JuNette's Cafe & Club" (https://acklinscreeksidebonefishlodge.com/, accessed 2026-10-03).
jewels.booking_route: through the lodge ((242) 357-4179)

jewels.name: Seaview Bay
jewels.blurb: "The beaches here are stunning, and often, yours and yours alone. Try North Side Beach, on Long Cay, or perhaps Seaview Bay on Crooked Island."
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free public beach

jewels.name: North Side Beach
jewels.blurb: On Long Cay: "Come and see the clear white sand and crystal clear water." The Long Cay listing adds "there are great secluded beaches on the cays north side, with crystal clear water and clean white sand" (https://www.bahamas.com/plan-your-trip/things-to-do/long-cay, accessed 2026-10-03).
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free public beach

jewels.name: Lovely Bay Beach
jewels.blurb: Named among the island's beaches on the official site; Lovely Bay is one of Acklins' two largest settlements, "Lovely Bay in the northwestern tip of the island" (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acklins, accessed 2026-10-03).
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free public beach

jewels.name: Colonel Hill
jewels.blurb: "This settlement has the highest point on the island, with an unmatched view. It is home to the Central and Local Government offices, Post Office and Police Station, plus Central Park, a community park that is the site of homecomings and other major events."
jewels.booking_route: none needed - public settlement

jewels.name: Spring Point and the Outside Kitchen
jewels.blurb: "This is Acklins capital and the location of Outside Kitchen, a stonehouse ruin smothered by flowering bushes."
jewels.booking_route: none needed - public settlement

jewels.name: Airport Inn Restaurant & Bar
jewels.blurb: "A charming restaurant that overlooks the airport offering delicious Bahamian dishes and native delicacies. Breakfast, lunch and dinner is served daily." Spring Point; Mrs. Mable E. Hanna.
jewels.booking_route: phone/email only ((242) 344-3600, acklinsairportinn@outlook.com)

jewels.name: Seaside Restaurant and Bar
jewels.blurb: Listed by the official site for Acklins & Crooked Island at General Delivery, Lovely Bay; Ms. Claudine Virgil. The listing carries no description or menu.

jewels.name: Aardvark McLeod - Crooked Island Trophy Lodge
jewels.blurb: UK fly-fishing agent selling the Trophy Lodge: "simple and comfortable", placed for "the best areas of Crooked Island and Acklins in the same week"; capacity 10 guests; guides "All natives of the atoll"; bonefish average "around 4 pounds; island record is 17.6lb"; season "January through June, November through December".
jewels.booking_route: agent - Alex Jardine or Charlotte Chilcott, +44 (0)1980 847389, or the page's Book Now link

jewels.name: Fish Partner - Crooked & Acklins Islands Trophy Lodge
jewels.blurb: Reykjavik fly-fishing outfitter selling the Trophy Lodge with published packages: "4 nights / 3 days package base 2 : $1990/person"; "7 nights / 6 days package base 2 : $3690/person"; prices "included 12% of VAT". "The record bonefish caught on the island went 17,6 lbs!"
jewels.booking_route: agent - contact form on the page; (+354) 571 4545

jewels.name: Bahamasair (Nassau to Colonel Hill)
jewels.blurb: "Bahamas Air services the island from Nassau twice each week, Wednesdays and Saturdays. Bahamas Air lands at Colonel Hill (MYCI) airport" - as stated by Crooked Island Lodge. Carib Journal reports "several flights a week to Acklins' Spring Point Airport" (https://www.caribjournal.com/2025/06/17/bahamas-acklins-island, accessed 2026-10-03). The carrier's own homepage, read 2026-10-03, does not list either route.
jewels.booking_route: own website booking (bahamasair.com)

jewels.name: Scavella Enterprises
jewels.blurb: Named by the official site as one of three ways to reach Bird Rock Lighthouse: "Chartered boat tours to the island can be arranged through Crooked Island Lodge, Scavella Enterprises, and/or local fishing guides." No own page or contact was found.
jewels.booking_route: not stated - no contact on the page read

faq.q: How do I get to Acklins Island?
faq.a: Fly to Nassau first, then on to Acklins: Bahamasair operates "several flights a week to Acklins' Spring Point Airport". Crooked Island, across the Bight, is reachable "by twice-daily ferries from Acklins" (https://www.bahamas.com/islands/acklins-crooked-island, accessed 2026-10-03).

faq.q: Where is Acklins Island?
faq.a: In the southern Bahamas, "385 km (239 mi) Southeast of Nassau". It is "one of a group of islands arranged along a large, shallow lagoon called the Bight of Acklins", with Crooked Island in the north and Acklins in the southeast.

faq.q: How far is Acklins from Nassau?
faq.a: Acklins lies "385 km (239 mi) Southeast of Nassau".

faq.q: What is the Acklins airport code?
faq.a: Spring Point Airport on Acklins is AXP on the official site's island map. Crooked Island has Colonel Hill (CRI) and Pitts Town Point (PWN). "This regional airport connects Acklins Island to neighboring Crooked Island and Nassau."

faq.q: What is the population of Acklins?
faq.a: 692 at the 2022 census (the article cites the Government of The Bahamas' 2022 preliminary census results); "The population of Acklins was 565 at the 2010 census, with the largest populations at Lovely Bay in the northwestern tip of the island and in Salina Point in the southernmost area of the island."

faq.q: What is Acklins known for?
faq.a: Bonefishing first: "The shallow waters of the Bight of Acklins and many winding flats make Acklins & Crooked Island one of the top spots for bonefishing in The Bahamas." Also its Lucayan past - "Pompey Bay Beach in Acklins is the site of one of the largest Lucayan settlements in The Bahamas" - and cascarilla: "Acklins Island is one of only two islands in The Bahamas where Cascarilla Bark grows", exported "as the main ingredient in Campari Liquor."

faq.q: What is bonefishing like on Acklins Island?
faq.a: Acklins Creekside Bonefish Lodge: "Bone-fishing flats are untouched in this area with an average weight of 4-9 pound fish." "Wade fishing directly across from the lodge is also a great option." A flats licence is needed: "All anglers over the age of 12 will need a license to fish", from "$15.00" for a day.

faq.q: What is Acklins Creekside Bonefish Lodge?
faq.a: A lodge at Chester's Bay, Acklins: "Just 50 paces from your bed, you can step into a three-mile, ankle-to-knee-deep flat for kayaking, wading, and DIY bone fishing." Rooms have "two standard beds, private bath"; guests dine at JuNette's Café & Club House. "The nightly hotel rate includes airport transfers, all meals, snacks, and soft drinks". Contact (242) 357-4179.

faq.q: What are Acklins and Crooked Island?
faq.a: "This small atoll includes the islands of Acklins, Crooked Island and Long Cay, wrapped around the Bight of Acklins." Acklins is "The largest island in the group"; Crooked Island "is reachable by air, via the Colonel Hill Airport, or by twice-daily ferries from Acklins"; Long Cay "is only 8 sq miles".

faq.q: What hotels are there on Acklins, Bahamas?
faq.a: Fishing lodges rather than hotels. On Acklins the official site lists Acklins Creekside Bonefish Lodge (https://www.bahamas.com/hotels/acklins-creekside-bonefish-lodge) and Grey's Point Bonefish Inn, "located in the heart of Acklins' fishing grounds"; across the Bight on Crooked Island are the Crooked & Acklins Island Trophy Lodge (https://www.bahamas.com/hotels/crooked-acklins-trophy-lodge) and Crooked Island Lodge & Marina (https://www.crookedislandlodge.com/), all accessed 2026-10-03.

name: The Berry Islands
line: About 30 cays and a seven-mile beach

jewels.name: Great Harbour Cay Beach
jewels.blurb: "Roughly 7 miles long and 2.5 miles at its widest point, Great Harbour Cay in The Berry Islands is known for its welcoming atmosphere and white sand beaches" with "ultra-romantic scenery, crystal clear waters, peace and quiet." The Out Islands board lists "Seven continuous miles of beautiful beaches and a protected harbor" (https://www.myoutislands.com/bahamas-islands/berry-islands/beaches, accessed 2026-10-03).
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free public beach

jewels.name: Chub Cay Resort & Marina
jewels.blurb: "This private island paradise sits at the southern tip of The Berry Islands. It is a sport fisherman's and diver's dream location, at the edge of 'The Pocket'" (https://www.bahamas.com/hotels/chub-cay-club, accessed 2026-10-03). Its own site lists 11 Clubhouse Suites, 8 Beach Cabanas and 18 Private Villas, "108 slips, vessels to 160'" and customs and fuel "daily 7am-7pm". ⛔ "Chub Cay is a private island club. Port-of-entry services are limited; the rest of the island is members-only" (https://www.chubcay.com/visit, accessed 2026-10-03).
jewels.booking_route: members reserve through the member portal; visitors phone (786) 209-0025, VHF 68 or info@chubcay.com - "Contact and written permission are required before entering"

jewels.name: Hoffman's Cay Blue Hole
jewels.blurb: "A popular spot for travellers, Hoffman's Cay Blue Hole is 600 ft wide with a cliff that hangs 20 feet above the water. Jump off and dive into this unique natural wonder. Nearby, you may also stumble upon The Hoffman Cay Ruins, a peculiar rock structure echoing ghosts of the past." Reached by boat; The Right Choice runs "tours to the Blue Hole".
jewels.booking_route: none needed - an uninhabited natural site; boat access through a tour operator

jewels.name: Chub Cay sportfishing and the 2027 tournaments
jewels.blurb: "Billfish Capital of the Bahamas": The Pocket has "marlin and sailfish in abundance, plus wahoo, mahi, and tuna"; the north-side flats are "some of the best bonefishing in the world"; charters with "experienced captains" from the marina. Published 2027 dates: Winter Wahoo Shootout Jan 21-23 (members only, $3,500 + VAT), Classic Feb 18-20 and Open Mar 11-13 (open to public, $5,000 + VAT each), Invitational Apr 1-3 (members only, $5,000 + VAT).
jewels.booking_route: own website tournament inquiry form; charters through the marina

jewels.name: Great Harbour Cay bonefish flats
jewels.blurb: "Head to the saltwater flats of Great Harbour Cay - or most any flat across the archipelago - and match wits with the elusive grey ghost." The Out Islands board: bonefish schools "in the thousands", fished in creeks on Great Harbour Cay, on beaches and uninhabited cays further south, and "catch and release" rules apply in the Out Islands (https://myoutislands.com/blog/boi-news/king-of-the-flats-conquer-bonefishing-in-the-berrys, accessed 2026-10-03).
jewels.booking_route: none needed to see the flats; fishing through a licensed guide or lodge

jewels.name: Chub Cay Wall
jewels.blurb: "A continuous wall stretching from Chub Cay to Whale Cay and dropping to a depth of nearly 4,000 feet, the Chub Cay Wall offers divers a high-visibility glimpse at Caribbean reef sharks, spotted eagle rays, and abundant black coral."
jewels.booking_route: none needed - a natural dive site; dives sold by Chub Cay Divers to Chub Cay guests

jewels.name: Chub Cay Divers
jewels.blurb: "A watersports and island tour center, offering our services exclusively to guests of Chub Cay Resort & Marina"; PADI Five Star Dive Resort; reefs "5 minutes from the marina", snorkelling, paddleboarding at Turtle Creek, a Blue Hole trip with rock jumping, and sandbar visits.
jewels.booking_route: phone/email only (+1 (242) 809-5574, contact@chubcaydivers.com) - Chub Cay guests only

jewels.name: Soul Fly Lodge
jewels.blurb: "A consciously Crafted Bahamas fly fishing experience": guided permit and bonefish fly fishing from Maverick HPX-V skiffs, up to 6 rooms and 8 anglers on 4 boats, "minutes from the runway" at Great Harbour Cay. Packages include "guided fishing, lodging, all meals, beverages, airport transfers"; per person $3,365-$7,585 double, up to $12,520 for "Single Everything", and "Primo Permit" 6 days/7 nights single $19,750; "10% VAT not included; airfare and tips excluded."
jewels.booking_route: own website contact form, kyle@soulflylodge.com, WhatsApp (603) 969-3050 or (207) 630-6211; 50% deposit within 10 days, balance 60 days before arrival

jewels.name: Carriearl Boutique Hotel and Restaurant
jewels.blurb: The Out Islands board: Carriearl "features four ensuite bedrooms" and is a social hub with a restaurant and cocktail lounge; its "Tasty Tingums" plate is lobster and shrimp tempura, calamari and cracked conch; it provides a free shuttle for boaters at Great Harbour Cay Marina. Its own site (carriearl.com) returned HTTP 522 when read.
jewels.booking_route: not observed - the hotel's own site did not load when read

jewels.name: Flo's Conch Bar
jewels.blurb: "Little Harbour is home to Flo's Conch Bar, a local landmark favored by passing boaters" (https://www.bahamas.com/islands/berry-islands). Its listing: "We are world renowned for our Bahamian seafood, especially 'conchy' conch fritters and other specialties, plus Chester's Rum Punch from his own secret recipe, and panoramic ocean views." Hours "12:00 noon Until for Lunch and Dinner".

jewels.name: The New Beach Club ("Da Beach Club")
jewels.blurb: "Also known as 'Da Beach Club', we are located just above the tranquil beach shore, and across from the Great Harbour Cay Airport." Hours: "Tuesday through Sunday / Breakfast 8:00 a.m.-11:00 a.m. / Lunch 11:00 a.m.-3:30 p.m." Yachting magazine: "a popular midday stop for lunch and a drink" (https://www.yachtingmagazine.com/cruising-and-chartering/island-icon-berry-islands/, accessed 2026-10-03).

jewels.name: Chub Cay Clubhouse Restaurant
jewels.blurb: "Breakfast, lunch and dinner - local flavors, traditional favorites, and fresh daily specials", with "outdoor seating on the terrace overlooking the infinity pool and Bahamian sunsets" and holiday menus for Thanksgiving, Christmas Day and New Year's Eve. ⛔ "clubhouse restaurant and bar are for members"; non-member property owners may use The Nauti Rooster Bar & Grill for a fee.
jewels.booking_route: members only - (786) 209-0025 or info@chubcay.com

jewels.name: The Right Choice (boat tours and water taxi)
jewels.blurb: "We are the right choice for viewing the underwater treasures of The Berry Islands by glassbottom boat and speed boat. We also offer water taxi service, tours to the Blue Hole, and excursions to cays within the chain and to other islands of The Bahamas." Contact: Mr. Cardinal Rolle, Great Harbour Cay.
jewels.booking_route: phone/email only ((242) 367-8145, cardyrolle@hotmail.com)

jewels.name: Percy Darville, bonefishing guide
jewels.blurb: "One of the most well known local faces on the bonefishing circuit" in the Berry Islands; his family has lived in the area for over 100 years. Named by the Out Islands board; no contact details were printed on the page read.
jewels.booking_route: not observed - no booking route printed on the page read

jewels.name: Great Harbour Cay Marina
jewels.blurb: "The cay's well-protected namesake hurricane hole marina, a port of entry", with "65 slips and can accommodate yachts up to 150 feet" (Yachting, April 25, 2024). The Out Islands board's bonefishing article names Great Harbour Cay Marina as where private boats can dock (https://myoutislands.com/blog/boi-news/king-of-the-flats-conquer-bonefishing-in-the-berrys, accessed 2026-10-03). greatharbourcaymarina.com returned HTTP 404 when read, so this is a guide-site source.
jewels.booking_route: not observed - the marina's own site did not load when read

jewels.name: Shelling Beach, Sand Dollar Hill and Sugar Beach
jewels.blurb: "Shelling Beach, Sand Dollar Hill, Sugar Beach - even the names of the beaches are irresistible. Across the Berry Islands' 30-cay cluster, discover a pristine and secluded stretch of powder-soft sand that seems made for beachcombing." Yachting: Sugar Beach "often ranks as one the prettiest beaches in the Bahamas. Its caves entice visitors to explore" (https://www.yachtingmagazine.com/cruising-and-chartering/island-icon-berry-islands/, accessed 2026-10-03).
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free public beaches

jewels.name: Shark Creek Beach
jewels.blurb: A "wide, shallow" beach on Great Harbour Cay that "attracts shell collectors and nature lovers" (Yachting, April 25, 2024); also on the Out Islands board's Berry Islands beach list.
jewels.booking_route: none needed - free public beach

jewels.name: Great Stirrup Cay Lighthouse
jewels.blurb: "This 268-acre cay has been privately owned by Norwegian Cruise Line since 1977 and is the site of the Great Stirrup Cay Lighthouse" (bahamas.com). The Out Islands board: "an 1863 lighthouse", and Williamstown, "now abandoned", established "during the reign of William IV" (https://www.myoutislands.com/bahamas-islands/berry-islands/landmarks-attractions, accessed 2026-10-03). ⛔ Seen from the water or by cruise; the cay is private.
jewels.booking_route: none - a private cay; no public access route stated

faq.q: How do I get to the Berry Islands, Bahamas?
faq.a: By air or by private boat. Makers Air flies from Fort Lauderdale Executive (FXE) to Great Harbour Cay with "Scheduled Service: Daily" and to Chub Cay "Mondays, Fridays", plus private charters daily. The Out Islands board also lists LeAir and Bahamasair from Nassau to Great Harbour Cay, and Aztec Airways and Tropic Ocean Airways from Fort Lauderdale. Boaters can clear customs at Chub Cay "daily 7am-7pm" after obtaining written permission.

faq.q: What airport serves the Berry Islands, Bahamas?
faq.a: Two main airports: "Great Harbour Cay Airport welcomes domestic flights via Nassau" and "Chub Cay International Airport is often the gateway to the Berry Islands for international travellers, located just 45 minutes by plane from South Florida." Big Whale Cay also has an airport.

faq.q: Where are the Berry Islands?
faq.a: In The Bahamas: "a cluster of 30 cays, southeast of Bimini", per the Bahamas Out Islands Promotion Board. Chub Cay sits at the southern tip, and its airport is "45 minutes by plane from South Florida" (bahamas.com).

faq.q: What are the Berry Islands known for?
faq.a: Fishing and the water. The official site leads with "Unparalleled big game fishing" and says "Two things are required in The Berry Islands: a boat and a love of water." Chub Cay is "The Billfish Capital of The Bahamas", Great Harbour Cay's flats are for bonefishing, and Hoffman's Cay Blue Hole "is 600 ft wide with a cliff that hangs 20 feet above the water."

faq.q: What are the things to do in the Berry Islands, Bahamas?
faq.a: The official site names big-game fishing, bonefishing on "the saltwater flats of Great Harbour Cay", diving the Chub Cay Wall ("Caribbean reef sharks, spotted eagle rays, and abundant black coral"), jumping into Hoffman's Cay Blue Hole, beachcombing at Shelling Beach, Sand Dollar Hill and Sugar Beach, and lunch at Flo's Conch Bar on Little Harbour Cay.

faq.q: Is CocoCay in the Berry Islands?
faq.a: Yes. bahamas.com lists Little Stirrup Cay among The Berry Islands: "Also known as Coco Cay, this private island is a port of call for Royal Caribbean International Cruises." Royal Caribbean's Perfect Day at CocoCay is for its cruise guests only.

faq.q: What is the population of the Berry Islands, Bahamas?
faq.a: About 700 residents, most of them at Bullock's Harbour and Great Harbour Cay, according to the Bahamas Out Islands Promotion Board.

faq.q: What hotels are in the Berry Islands, Bahamas?
faq.a: Three were sourced for this build: Chub Cay Resort & Marina (Clubhouse Suites, Beach Cabanas and Private Villas - a private club where "the rest of the island is members-only"), Soul Fly Lodge, an all-inclusive fly-fishing lodge of up to 6 rooms at Great Harbour Cay, and Carriearl Boutique Hotel with four ensuite bedrooms. This answer quotes Soul Fly's own page: "guided fishing, lodging, all meals, beverages, airport transfers".

faq.q: What is the weather like in the Berry Islands?
faq.a: No Berry Islands climate table was read for this build. What NOAA states for the whole basin: "The Atlantic hurricane season runs from June 1 to November 30." "The peak of the Atlantic hurricane season is September 10, with most activity occurring between mid-August and mid-October."

faq.q: Where can I stay in Inagua, Bahamas?
faq.a: The Ministry of Tourism lists Malley Suites on Meadow Street, Matthew Town, which "opened in 2012 to help meet the demands of short-term visitors to Inagua", with three one-bedroom apartments with full kitchens and one with a kitchenette, booked by email to Mr. Ransford Malcolm. No rate is published.

faq.q: What is there to do in Inagua, Bahamas?
faq.a: The Ministry of Tourism points to the flamingos and over 140 bird species, the Great Inagua Lighthouse in Matthew Town (climb it for "panoramic views of Inagua and Cuba to the southwest" on a clear day), Union Creek Reserve's turtle research, Little Inagua by boat, snook fishing and bonefish flats.

faq.q: Where is Inagua located in the Bahamas?
faq.a: At the very south. The Ministry of Tourism calls it "The southernmost island in The Bahamas" and "The third largest island in The Bahamas, Great Inagua stretches 20 miles long"; its neighbour Little Inagua is "the largest uninhabited cay in the Caribbean".

faq.q: What is the airport at Matthew Town, Inagua?
faq.a: Inagua International Airport (IGA) in Matthew Town. The Ministry of Tourism: "Great Inagua is most commonly reached through Great Inagua Airport" and "Located in Inagua's Matthew Town, Inagua International Airport services domestic routes".

faq.q: What is the Inagua woodstar?
faq.a: A hummingbird found on Inagua. The Ministry of Tourism: "In 2015 they were classified as an entirely different species; now they are known as the Inagua woodstar." Certified birding guides in Matthew Town lead tours to see it.

faq.q: Is Great Inagua inhabited?
faq.a: Yes, at one settlement. The Ministry of Tourism: "The only settlement on Great Inagua, Matthew Town, was once a bustling cosmopolitan city. Today, it's considerably quieter, but its robust salt industry dates back centuries."

faq.q: What is Morton Salt on Inagua, Bahamas?
faq.a: The Bahamas National Trust says Morton Salt Bahamas has "supported the BNT and flamingo conservation for decades": its saltpans give flamingos feeding habitat through naturally occurring brine shrimp, and it provides office space and maintains access roads to the park.

faq.q: How do I get to Mayaguana?
faq.a: By air on Bahamasair from Nassau. Its booking engine lists the Nassau (NAS) - Mayaguana (MYG) route; for the week of October 4-10, 2026 it showed one flight, UP-425 on Monday October 5, departing Nassau 9:30 AM and arriving 12:15 PM with "1 Stop". Check the carrier for your own dates.

faq.q: What is Mayaguana's airport code?
faq.a: MYG. The Ministry of Tourism: Mayaguana Airport (MYG), "Located near Abraham's Bay, it is the only airport serving the island with regularly scheduled service to Nassau."

faq.q: Does Mayaguana have a new airport?
faq.a: A new terminal. The Tribune reported (March 2, 2026) that the Prime Minister opened a $2.1 million terminal on February 27, 2026: "just under 3,200 square feet", fully air-conditioned, with ticketing, 30-passenger seating, baggage screening and a police station, on a 6,700-foot runway.

faq.q: What is the Mayaguana port project?
faq.a: A planned cruise and cargo port, in three phases: a temporary marine offloading facility and deep-water port, then a cruise ship terminal, then a deep-water transshipment port. It is owned by the Government of The Bahamas, the Mayaguana Island Development Fund and Global Lead Consultant Group Limited, operated by Mayaguana Port Group Ltd., and as of April 22, 2026 was "expected to move into detailed planning in the coming months". It is not built.

faq.q: Where should I stay in Mayaguana, Bahamas?
faq.a: The one hotel listed by the Ministry of Tourism is the Mayaguana Baycaner Beach Resort on Baycaner Avenue: "Our 16-room hotel is located in a corner of a quiet beach, and your room is just steps away from it." It books by phone, (242) 339-3726, or baycanerbeach@gmail.com.

faq.q: What is Mayaguana known for?
faq.a: Solitude, fishing and reefs. The Ministry of Tourism calls it "More isolated and less developed than any other island in The Bahamas" and "A Pirate Stronghold Turned Prized Fishing Spot", and says "Mayaguana is the only island in The Bahamas that conserves its original Arawak name."

faq.q: How far is Mayaguana from Nassau?
faq.a: About 560 km (350 mi): Mayaguana is "About 100 km (62 mi) north of Great Inagua and 560 km (350 mi) southeast of the capital Nassau".

faq.q: How far is Mayaguana from Turks and Caicos?
faq.a: About 100 km (62 mi). Settlement began in 1812, "when people began to migrate from the Turks and Caicos Islands, which are located about 100 km (62 mi) southeast."

faq.q: What is the population of Mayaguana?
faq.a: 208 in the 2022 census, as given in the Wikipedia infobox (citing the Government's preliminary 2022 census results); the 2010 census counted 277.

faq.q: How big is Mayaguana?
faq.a: "It has an area of about 280 km2 (110 sq mi)", and it is "the easternmost island and district of The Bahamas".

faq.q: What is Ragged Island known for?
faq.a: Bonefishing. "There's more bonefish than people on Ragged Island Bahamas, hence why it's known as a fisherman's paradise." The official site also names its salt ponds - residents "still harvest salt from their family plots" - its boat builders, and the one church where "members of three different religious denominations gather" on Sundays.

faq.q: Where is Ragged Island, Bahamas?
faq.a: At the southern end of the Jumentos chain: "Great and Little Ragged Island lie at the end of a chain of islets, cays, and rocks that stretch over 100 miles." Its one settlement is Duncan Town. Lost Key Lodge places the island 60 miles north of Cuba (https://lostkeylodge.com/, accessed 2026-10-03).

faq.q: How do I get to Ragged Island, Bahamas?
faq.a: By charter flight or boat. The official site: "The Duncan Town Airport is the only airport servicing Ragged Island" and "most travellers stay in nearby Long Island and venture over for a day, via boat or charter flight." Lost Key Lodge routes its anglers through Georgetown, Exuma ("American Airlines is very convenient out of Atlanta") and arranges a charter to Duncan Town at "$850 per person round trip" (https://lostkeylodge.com/pricing-and-availability, accessed 2026-10-03).

faq.q: Does Ragged Island, Bahamas have an airport?
faq.a: Yes: "The Duncan Town Airport is the only airport servicing Ragged Island." No scheduled airline route to it was found - Bahamasair's homepage does not list it (https://www.bahamasair.com/, accessed 2026-10-03) - and visitors arrive by charter flight.

faq.q: Are there hotels on Ragged Island, Bahamas?
faq.a: One fishing lodge was found. Lost Key Lodge takes "4 anglers maximum" on a "7 nights 6 days of fishing" package at $4,995.00 (https://lostkeylodge.com/pricing-and-availability, accessed 2026-10-03). For other visitors, the official site says "most travellers stay in nearby Long Island and venture over for a day, via boat or charter flight."

faq.q: What is the fishing like on Ragged Island, Bahamas?
faq.a: Flats and offshore. "The island is a haven for avid fishermen, with its unparalleled flats ideal for bonefishing", and "It's not uncommon to snag an abundance of grouper, snapper, barracuda, tuna, and kingfish during a one-day expedition on the water." Local guide Alvin Munroe says "There is great bonefishing on the west side of the mainland and the cays" (https://www.bahamas.com/vendor/alvin-munroe, accessed 2026-10-03).

faq.q: What is the population of Ragged Island, Bahamas?
faq.a: The 2022 census recorded 44 residents, down from 72 in 2010. A March 2024 visit reported "The 65 residents are served by electricity from BEC, a reverse osmosis plant for water, roads and an airstrip" (https://www.bahamianproject.com/2024/08/exuma-ragged-island-mailboat/, accessed 2026-10-03).

faq.q: What is the history of Ragged Island, Bahamas?
faq.a: Salt, then storm. The salt ponds were "developed in the 19th century by Duncan Taylor and his brother Major Taylor", and Duncan Town is named for him (https://www.bahamas.com/vendor/ragged-island-salt-ponds, accessed 2026-10-03). The industry peaked in the 1930s before declining. On 8 September 2017 Hurricane Irma struck Duncan Town directly and the prime minister ordered an evacuation; a solar farm completed by February 2020 was built to supply "at least 90% of the island's energy needs."

faq.q: What is the weather like on Ragged Island, Bahamas?
faq.a: The island sits in the Atlantic hurricane belt: "The Atlantic hurricane season runs from June 1 to November 30." "The peak of the Atlantic hurricane season is September 10, with most activity occurring between mid-August and mid-October." Hurricane Irma struck Duncan Town on 8 September 2017.

jewels.name: Columbus Monument, Long Bay
jewels.blurb: "This monument to Columbus landfall is located at Long Bay, so named for Columbus long boat. This is the point where he came ashore. A monument placed on the floor of the ocean in Long Bay marks the exact spot where Columbus dropped anchor on October 12th, 1492. On the beach, a simple white cross commemorates the first land discovered in the West Indies." The cross, "erected by Columbian historian Ruth D. Wolper and the people of San Salvador in 1956, is the most photographed spot on the island."
jewels.booking_route: none needed - public monument on the beach

jewels.name: Riding Rock Resort & Marina
jewels.blurb: "Built, owned and operated by the William's family since the 1960's"; 22 rooms (18 deluxe in a two-storey building, 4 oceanfront in a single-storey one), "custom designed for dive travelers, with all of the diving facilities close at hand". Published 2026 all-inclusive dive packages run from $1,051 (5 days, quad) to $2,711 (8 days, single), including "Accommodations, meals, San Salvador Airport transfers to/from the resort and all taxes" (https://www.ridingrock.com/rates-package/, accessed 2026-10-03).
jewels.booking_route: phone/email only (800.272.1492, 242.331.2631, reservations@RidingRock.com) plus an online enquiry form

jewels.name: Club Med Columbus Isle
jewels.blurb: An all-inclusive resort on 89 acres; the package covers "accommodations, unlimited gourmet dining and drinks (alcoholic and non-alcoholic), and access to 25+ included activities" including sailing, snorkelling and paddleboarding; rooms are "brightly coloured, heritage-style bungalows with charming Creole design touches". Scuba diving is extra, with a diving doctor on site; Junior Club Med is named for July-August.
jewels.booking_route: own website booking or +1 (888) 932-2582; travel advisors book through the Club Med Travel Advisors portal (cmta.pro.clubmed)

jewels.name: Guanahani Divers
jewels.blurb: Riding Rock's dive operation: "Both boats are suitable for 20 divers"; "Scalloped Hammerheads being a favorite with visiting divers", "regularly seen in our waters in the cooler winter months"; extra boat dives "$50.00 per dive, provided we have a minimum of 6 divers". Its site guide names 20 sites, among them Telephone Pole ("photographed since 1974"), Devil's Claw's double wall and Runway 10, where hammerheads are occasionally seen (https://www.ridingrock.com/san-salvador-dive-sites/, accessed 2026-10-03).
jewels.booking_route: with the resort: 800.272.1492 or reservations@RidingRock.com; dives are bundled into Riding Rock's dive packages

jewels.name: Dixon Hill Lighthouse
jewels.blurb: "Built in 1887 on a former plantation owned by John Dixon, this lighthouse is still occupied and operated by lighthouse keepers who refuel the 400,000 candle powered lighthouse by hand every 2 hours and 15 minutes." Listed phone (242) 331-2227.
jewels.booking_route: none listed - bahamas.com gives a phone number, (242) 331-2227, and no admission

jewels.name: Grotto Beach, Sandy Point
jewels.blurb: Named first under "Find A Sandy Stretch" on the official island page: "Grotto Beach at Sandy Point". Sandy Point Cave and Double Cave dive sites lie off this coast (https://myoutislands.com/bahamas-diving/san-salvador-diving, accessed 2026-10-03).
jewels.booking_route: none needed - public beach

jewels.name: Great Lake National Park
jewels.blurb: "San Salvador is known as 'The Land of Lakes'. In the center of the island is the Great Lake, which served as the major means of transportation in days past. This is a protected body of water, in order to preserve its natural pristine wonder for future generations."
jewels.booking_route: none needed - protected public lake

jewels.name: Riding Rock Marina
jewels.blurb: "Twenty-five slips are available, accommodating boats up to 160 feet with advanced notice." "Draft at the marina entrance is 8 feet at low tide and 12 feet at high tide." "The fuel dock is open all year for diesel, gasoline and ice", 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Sunday-Friday. Dockage published at $3.00 per foot per day.
jewels.booking_route: phone/email only (800.272.1492, 242.331.2631, reservations@RidingRock.com)

jewels.name: Odyssey III deep-sea fishing charter (Riding Rock)
jewels.blurb: Riding Rock's 28-foot charter boat: "1/2 Day (4 Hours) $800" and "Full Day (8 Hours) $1200" per vessel, maximum 5 persons; "Tackle, bait, and water are provided"; targets Blue Marlin, Wahoo, Dolphin, Kingfish and Tuna, and the resort encourages "catch and release sport fishing in an effort towards conservation".
jewels.booking_route: phone/email only (800.272.1492, 242.331.2631, reservations@RidingRock.com)

jewels.name: Guanahani Beach Club Resort
jewels.blurb: "Our secluded property is located on the southeast coast of San Salvador, just 15 minutes from the San Salvador International" airport; private villas, the Patio Restaurant Bar, a Surf & Sail Center with catamaran sailing, diving, kayaking and kitesurfing, at Sunrise Road, Snowy Bay, Sandy Point. jewels.name: The Chicago Herald Monument
jewels.blurb: "The 1892 Worlds Fair, held in Chicago, celebrated the 400th anniversary of the discovery of the New World. In 1891, the Chicago Herald, an American newspaper, erected this sphere (hewn from native limestone) in commemoration of Columbus landfall."
jewels.booking_route: none needed - public monument

Guanahani Beach Club lists its address as Snowy Bay, Sandy Point (https://www.bahamas.com/hotels/guanahani-beach-club-resort, accessed 2026-10-03).

Club Med's Christopher Restaurant gives its address as Bonefish Bay, Cockburn Town (https://www.bahamas.com/vendor/christopher-restaurant, accessed 2026-10-03), and the Frasgate wreck lies "off Bonefish Bay" (https://myoutislands.com/bahamas-diving/san-salvador-diving, accessed 2026-10-03).
jewels.booking_route: none needed - public beach

jewels.name: Watling's Blue Hole
jewels.blurb: "Watling's Blue Hole, southwestern San Salvador Island" - "a popular spot among researchers interested in the categories of soluble rocks in The Bahamas": large water-filled, subcylindrical voids that extend well below sea level.
jewels.booking_route: none listed - a natural site; the official page names no access fee or operator

jewels.name: Gerace Research Centre
jewels.blurb: "The Gerace Research Center, formerly the Bahamian Field Station, occupies an old U.S. Navy base at Graham's Harbour on San Salvador's northern coast", working in archaeology, biology, geology and marine science for over 50 years and supporting conservation of the endangered San Salvador rock iguana. Its own site lists "separate housing for undergraduates, graduate students, faculty and researchers", field courses, and "SCUBA tanks are available for rent" (https://www.geraceresearchcentre.com/facilities.html, accessed 2026-10-03).

faq.q: How do I get to San Salvador, Bahamas?
faq.a: By air. The official tourism site says "San Salvador Airport (ZSA)" is "the island's only airport" and "welcomes international and domestic arrivals". No ferry or mail-boat service to San Salvador is described on the official getting-here page.

faq.q: Which airlines fly to San Salvador, Bahamas?
faq.a: Wikipedia's airport page lists Bahamasair to "Deadman's Cay, Miami, Nassau, Rock Sound", Air Canada Rouge to "Montréal–Trudeau" and Air Caraïbes "Seasonal: Paris–Orly". Check the carrier for current schedules; none was read on a carrier's own page.

faq.q: What is the San Salvador, Bahamas airport code?
faq.a: ZSA. The official site names it "San Salvador Airport (ZSA)"; its ICAO code is "MYSM" (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Salvador_Airport, accessed 2026-10-03).

faq.q: What is San Salvador, Bahamas known for?
faq.a: Columbus's landfall and its diving. The official site calls it "a unique island with sparkling lakes, historic monuments, secluded beaches, and dive sites", with "50+ Dive Sites", and says Columbus's landing is marked by "a stone cross on San Salvador's Long Bay".

faq.q: What is there to do in San Salvador, Bahamas?
faq.a: The official island page lists beaches ("Grotto Beach at Sandy Point, Bonefish Bay Beach, and Snow Beach"), bays to anchor in ("Dim Bay, Long Bay, and Snow Bay"), "50+ Dive Sites" including "Devil's Claw, Vicky's Reef, and Runway 10", fishing for "blue marlin, wahoo, dolphin, kingfish, and tuna", the Columbus landfall cross, the Gerace Research Centre, Great Lake National Park and Watling's Blue Hole.

faq.q: Where should I stay in San Salvador, Bahamas?
faq.a: The official site says lodging ranges from "all-inclusive luxury villas to fully furnished beachfront cottages". The properties read for this dossier are Club Med Columbus Isle (all-inclusive), Riding Rock Resort & Marina (a dive resort with 22 rooms) and Guanahani Beach Club Resort (private villas at Snowy Bay, Sandy Point).

faq.q: Is there a Club Med in San Salvador, Bahamas?
faq.a: Yes: Club Med Columbus Isle, an all-inclusive resort on 89 acres. The package covers "accommodations, unlimited gourmet dining and drinks (alcoholic and non-alcoholic), and access to 25+ included activities"; scuba diving is extra.

faq.q: Are there all-inclusive resorts in San Salvador, Bahamas?
faq.a: Club Med Columbus Isle is all-inclusive. Riding Rock Resort & Marina also sells "All Inclusive Dive Vacation Packages" and non-diver packages that include "Accommodations, meals, San Salvador Airport transfers to/from the resort and all taxes" but exclude alcoholic drinks, sodas, bottled water and gratuities (https://www.ridingrock.com/rates-package/, accessed 2026-10-03).

faq.q: How big is San Salvador, Bahamas?
faq.a: San Salvador Island covers "163 km2 (63 sq mi)". The official tourism site adds that the island is "the exposed peak of a 15,000 ft mountain" (https://www.bahamas.com/islands/san-salvador, accessed 2026-10-03).

faq.q: What is the population of San Salvador, Bahamas?
faq.a: "The 2022 census recorded 824 residents", per Wikipedia's island article.
